question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(4)=-3,\,{f}^{′}(4)=-1,\,g(4)=2,\,{g}^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{4}
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=4.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x)) & =f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $x=4$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=4} & =f(4){g}^{′}(4)+g(4){f}^{′}(4) \\  & =(-3)\cdot \frac{1}{4}+2\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{11}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
